story: Gandhari, princess of Gandhara, married the blind king Dhritarashtra and blindfolded herself for life to share his darkness. She was the mother of the hundred Kauravas, including Duryodhana.
belief: She is honoured for her devotion and the spiritual power built up by years of sacrifice. Her blindfold is read both as loyalty and as a choice not to see.
turns: She never truly stopped her sons. After the war, in grief, she cursed Krishna that his clan would destroy itself in 36 years, and it came true.
facts: She lifted her blindfold once, to make Duryodhana's body invincible, but he was wearing a loincloth and his thighs stayed weak.
Gandhara covered parts of today's Pakistan and Afghanistan.
She outlived all hundred of her sons.
lessons: Love sometimes means opening your eyes.
Loyalty to a person shouldn't blind you to right and wrong.
Grief can harden into a curse; take care.
more: Her hundred sons were born from a mass of flesh that Vyasa divided into pots.
She also had a daughter, Dushala.
